findings.where: First screen: the line under the heading and the photograph of Mark at the lectern, with its caption; the same at phone width
findings.fault: Nothing on the first screen can be checked. The line under the heading says he advises development banks, agencies and governments, but it names no body, no region and no year. The photograph shows him speaking at an event, and its caption says only 'Placeholder', so the event is never named. The visitor is asked to write to him on his word alone, while the article specimen below does name its event ('An interview at the Belt and Road summit').
findings.who_objects: A development bank's procurement officer, arriving from LinkedIn to decide whether to shortlist him. They judge relevant experience by named bodies, regions and project kinds. A general claim with no specifics reads like any consultant's self-description, and they cannot confirm he is the person who did the work.

findings.where: First screen: the heading, 'In my view, we are at a turning point in the story of Public-Private Partnerships.'
findings.fault: The heading promises an argument (what the turning point is, and why it matters) that the page never makes and never links to. Nothing below the heading says what is changing. The page's footer note says the line comes from Blog No. 2 (2020), but the visitor is not shown this, so a six-year-old claim reads as a statement about now. Read alone, the opening line is a teaser with no way to follow it up.
findings.who_objects: The visiting agency staffer, who reads the largest words first to learn why this advisor matters. They find a claim with no follow-through and no way to read the reasoning behind it, so the line that should prove his judgement only states that he has a view.

findings.where: Below the article specimen: the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026'
findings.fault: His newest talk is dated but gives no venue or host, so the one sign of current standing names no one who invited him. The house rule asks for the newest article or talk to show its venue.
findings.who_objects: A bank officer looking for evidence that recognised bodies ask him to speak. 'Lecture' with a date is not something they can check, while a named host would act as third-party proof that no testimonial can give here.

findings.where: First screen: the solid house-blue contact block 'Write to me directly / Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com'
findings.fault: The v7 card asks for 'one quiet contact', but the contact is a large, fully saturated blue box. It is the loudest thing on the navy ground and pulls the eye away from Mark's face and his line, so it reads more like a sales button than a personal address.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first against a brief that says 'one quiet contact' and lists 'salesy' as a failure. A senior public-sector reader may also take a loud call to action as the hard sell of a vendor rather than the manner of an advisor.

findings.where: Navigation (Profile, Articles and talks, Blog) and the footer (mark, 'Mark M. Moseley · Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com')
findings.fault: The navigation has no 'Contact' label, and the footer has no current year or copyright. A visitor who scrolls past the hero, or lands on an article, has no labelled way to reach him and no sign that the site is kept up to date.
findings.who_objects: A reader who arrives on an article from a shared link and wants to get in touch, or wants to know the site is current. The house trust checklist asks for a contact label in the navigation and this year's copyright on every page.
